svg.title: Auth Architecture Decision Records
svg.desc: Visual ADR for the Nikharta Roop authentication architecture decisions.
svg.text: Auth Architecture Decisions
A visual ADR: what we chose, why it exists, and what future engineers should preserve.
ADR-001
OTP-first auth, no password
Mobile number is the primary identity. Signup and login use OTP challenges.
Reason: simpler Hindi/mobile-first UX and less password-management risk.
ADR-002
Signup does not create user immediately
/register only creates AuthOtp. /register/verify creates User after OTP success.
Reason: avoid unverified account rows and fake signup clutter.
ADR-003
Tokens are opaque and hashed in DB
Session and refresh tokens are random strings; PostgreSQL stores only hashes.
Reason: a database leak should not expose usable auth tokens.
ADR-004
HttpOnly cookies plus bearer fallback
Browser clients use cookies; API/mobile clients can use Authorization Bearer.
Reason: reduce XSS token exposure without breaking non-browser clients.
ADR-005
Refresh token rotation
Every refresh issues a new session token and a new refresh token.
Reason: old refresh tokens become useless after successful rotation.
ADR-006
Explicit session management
Users can list sessions, logout current session, and revoke one session.
Reason: supports multi-device control and clear audit trails.
Token entropy policy
sessionToken = 32 bytes / 256-bit entropy. refreshToken = 64 bytes / 512-bit entropy.
Avoid 300+ char tokens unless there is a specific protocol reason. Entropy matters more than raw string length.
Future note: add DB/Redis rate limiting and CSRF header validation before production launch.
